text:
Laura (Sales): Quick sync on ACME POC — they're stuck integrating our SDK + streaming handshake. Trying to land the demo tomorrow, can someone help triage?
Mike (SE): Sending logs now, they say the websocket closes immediately after auth. Got a sample trace?
Laura (Sales): Pasted customer logs in Confluence, but snippet: 
``n2026-03-20T14:02:01Z INFO handshake:start client_id=acme-poc
2026-03-20T14:02:01Z ERROR handshake:auth_failed code=403 reason=missing-credentials
```
Mike (SE): Looks like they're using long-lived API key in header + a proxy that strips Authorization on upgrade. Common cloud infra pitfall.
Nishit (Eng): Can they try ephemeral creds / short-lived token flow? We have a recommended pattern: preflight REST call to /v1/sessions -> return websocket token. This avoids headers being stripped.
Laura (Sales): They're asking if that approach affects streaming latency or token rate limits.
Nishit (Eng): Minimal latency impact — one extra RTT at connection time only. Token rate limits: ephemeral tokens are lightweight; for POC we can bump the quota temporarily. I can open a short-term override for acme-company.
Sarah (Security): Reminder: ACME's SEC questionnaire flagged KMS integration and audit log retention. Do we have a one-pager for POC that explains where logs are stored and how keys are used in Private vs Hosted?
Mike (SE): I have a checklist we usually send: KMS is customer-managed for Private; hosted uses envelope encryption with HSM-backed keys. Audit logs retained 90 days by default, longer with enterprise add-on. I'll attach the doc after this thread.
Laura (Sales): Pricing question from buyer: if we spin up Dedicated capacity for the week of demo to guarantee latency, can we do a short reserved term or a trial reserved bucket?
Nishit (Eng): For Dedicated we can do a short-term commit (7-14 days) as a trial in most regions; finance okayed pilot credits for verified deals. I'll coordinate with finance.
Laura (Sales): Awesome — also they need structured output example using function/tool calling to map user intents to JSON schema. Any quick sample we can share?
Mike (SE): Paste quick example, it's what we demo in SDKs: 
```
// pseudo example for tool-calling
const resp = await client.chat.completions.create({
  model: "redwood-instruct-1",
  input: "Create calendar invite",
  tools: [calendarTool],
  structured_output: true
});
// resp.output -> {"action":"create_event","params":{"title":"..."}}
```
Laura (Sales): Perfect. Can we include an example for the Rust SDK and the websocket connect flow? The buyer is using Rust microservices.
Nishit (Eng): I'll add a minimal Rust snippet for websocket handshake: 
```
// Rust pseudo
let token = fetch_session_token().await?;
let ws_url = format!("wss://inference.redwood.ai/v1/stream?token={}", token);
let (ws, _) = connect_async(ws_url).await?;
```
Mike (SE): Also call out proxy and ALB sticky headers — if they're terminating TLS at a proxy, need to preserve the upgrade headers or use token-in-query param as Nishit suggested.
Laura (Sales): Customer also raised a security blocker: they require SAML SSO to the console and SCIM for user provisioning to share usage dashboards. Is that on our enterprise checklist?
Sarah (Security): Yes, SAML + SCIM supported on Enterprise. There is a short setup guide. For POC we can do a scoped service account and share a read-only dashboard if they can't complete SSO before demo.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy to staging/region-us-west finished: 2026-03-20T13:58:00Z :white_check_mark:
Mike (SE): Action items: 1) Nishit to open transient Dedicated trial & provide Rust websocket snippet. 2) Mike will send KMS/audit one-pager. 3) Sarah to confirm SAML/SCIM setup timeline. 4) Laura to relay token-rate/latency note to buyer.
Laura (Sales): Thanks team — I'll update the buyer and schedule a short tech call tomorrow 9am PT. :thumbsup:
